transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… things at home have been getting to me. My in-laws moved in, and since then I’ve just been really on edge and worn out. I’m snapping at my wife, avoiding work calls I’d normally deal with right away… and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think clearly.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about different things in your life, even before your in-laws moved in?
No… not really. Before they moved in, I was handling things fine. This all started maybe a few weeks after they came and sort of… took over the house.
Since your in-laws moved in, have you felt down, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or felt like you’re not good enough?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in everything or anything like that. I’ve just been… not myself, I guess. As for feeling not good enough, I don’t really think about it that way.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or motivation since your in-laws moved in?

Yeah… my energy’s been pretty low. I feel worn down a lot, and getting myself to handle things takes more effort than it should. I’ve even been putting off calls I’d normally just deal with right away.
Have you found yourself worrying constantly about different things — like work, family, or the future — even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?
I don’t think it’s like that… not constantly about everything. It’s more just tied to what’s going on at home. I’m not sitting there worrying about the future for no reason.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or worried about a variety of things in your life, not just at home, like work, relationships, or other responsibilities?
Not really, no. I mean, work is work, and there’s always stuff to deal with, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious about a bunch of different things. It’s mostly… the situation at home.
Do you feel like you can't control or stop the worry you feel about the situation at home?

Yeah… I think so. I try to shut it off, but since they moved in it’s like I’m keyed up all the time. I get worn down and then I end up snapping at my wife, or avoiding calls I’d normally just handle. It’s… it’s been harder to control than I’d like to admit.
Have your feelings of being worn down and keyed up continued even when things at home are calm, or do they seem to only come up when there's tension around the house?

It mostly comes up around the house, when there’s tension with my in-laws being there. But… even when it’s quiet, I don’t fully settle down. I still feel keyed up and worn out, and it’s been affecting me more than I want to admit. I’ve snapped at my wife, avoided calls I’d usually handle, and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
If you spend time away from home, like going out for the day or traveling for work, do your feelings of being keyed up and worn down improve at all?

A little, maybe. If I’m away from the house, I’m not as on edge right in that moment. But it doesn’t really go away. I’m still worn down, and I’ll catch myself avoiding calls or not thinking clearly… like with that musician’s contract I almost messed up. It’s like I carry it with me.

When did these feelings of being keyed up and worn down start in relation to your in-laws moving in? Were you already feeling this way before they arrived, or did it clearly begin after they moved in?
I was doing pretty normal before they came. I mean… busy, sure, but I was handling things. This started after they moved in—within a few weeks, I’d say. Once it felt like they’d taken over the house.
Have you noticed these symptoms—being keyed up and worn down—affecting areas of your life outside of home, like work or social interactions, or do they mostly stay tied to the home situation?

It’s not just at home. Work’s been affected too. I nearly lost a musician’s contract, and my managing partner… he questioned whether I could still be trusted with major negotiations. At home, it’s gotten bad enough that my wife pushed for outside help.
Have your feelings of being keyed up and worn down improved at all over time, or have they stayed about the same since your in-laws moved in?
It’s been about the same, I guess. It’s only been around a month since they moved in, but… no, I wouldn’t say it’s really improved.
Outside of the situation at home, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about other everyday things like work tasks, social interactions, or minor responsibilities?

Mostly it’s tied to home, but it spills over. Work tasks I’d normally just handle… I’ve been avoiding calls, and I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight. Social stuff, minor things—I don’t know. It’s mainly that I feel keyed up and worn down since they moved in.
Are your feelings of being keyed up and worn down only in response to the situation with your in-laws, or do they also happen in other areas of your life even when that stressor isn't present?

It’s mostly because of my in-laws being in the house. That’s when all of this started. But it doesn’t just stay there… I carry it into work, avoid calls, and I almost let a contract fall apart because I couldn’t focus.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms began specifically after the in-laws moved in and are primarily tied to that stressor, with some spillover into work functioning. There is no evidence of persistent depression (ruling out F32.1), and the anxiety appears to be in response to a specific psychosocial stressor rather than being free-floating or excessive worry about multiple domains (ruling out F41.1). The symptoms have not improved and are causing significant impairment in multiple areas, consistent with F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood).
